commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
Add FLT to the DatedServiceJourney codespaces (#843)

Flytoget upgraded its NeTEx import to 1.16 and publishes DatedServiceJourney
replacements with the 1.16 structure (replacedJourneys/DatedVehicleJourneyRef).
FLT was not in netex.dsj.codespaces, so hasDsjReplacements() returned false and
both the legacy export and the legacy copy of the original dataset sent to Nisaba
were plain copies of the 1.16 dataset: outbound/netex-dsj-legacy/, the default
outbound/netex/ folder, the aggregated Norway export built from them, and the
imported/ and imported-dsj-legacy/ folders that nuska serves as the legacy
variant all carried replacedJourneys.

Production OTP reads the default folder with netex-java-model 2.0.15.4 and cannot
read that structure.

Verified in dev, where the property was patched in the config map ahead of this
change: the legacy variants of the 2026-09-21 FLT dataset are NeTEx 1.15 with
1 169 DatedServiceJourneyRef and no replacedJourneys, and the new variants are
unchanged 1.16 with 2 338 replacedJourneys.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
chore(renovate): keep Camel minor out of the aggregate PR (#841)

The shared ror-renovate-config extends group:allNonMajor, which folds
every minor and patch into the all-minor-patch aggregate PR. The
existing Camel rule only set automerge to false, so a Camel minor still
landed in that PR (see #816, Camel 4.21.0 -> 4.22.1).

Camel is not SemVer compliant, so a minor may carry breaking changes and
deserves to be reviewed and tested on its own. Override groupName for
Camel major and minor so they get a dedicated PR, leaving only Camel
patches in the aggregate. Both artifacts resolve camel.version, so they
are grouped together rather than ungrouped, which would produce two
branches editing the same line.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
Build the aggregated Norway export without recompressing it (#838)

* perf(netex): build the aggregated Norway export without recompressing it

The per-provider exports are already deflated and the aggregation only repackages them,
yet it unpacked all 62 onto disk and re-deflated the whole tree: 186 s on average, on the
critical path of every OTP2 graph build. RawZipMerger now copies the entries still
compressed with commons-compress, which takes a variant from 134.5 s to 1.3 s on the
production inputs with content-equal output. A corrupt export fails the merge with its
name, and the plan owns and closes its source archives.

* fix(netex): check the missing DSJ exports against the providers the aggregation read

direct:distributeMissingDsjNetexExports re-read the provider cache after
direct:otp2ExportMergedNetex had snapshotted it, so a provider dropping out of the cache
between the two reads was neither distributed nor recorded as missing, and both variants
were silently built without it. The distribution now checks the snapshot carried in the
exchange. The published-provider filter and the export file name are each defined once,
in BaseRouteBuilder and NetexDsjExportConfig.

* chore(netex): drop the stream caching of the merge route, whose body is a File

Stream caching only acts on InputStream bodies, and the body of direct:otp2MergeNetex has
been a java.io.File since before the raw copy. The flag never did anything.

* Improve Javadoc

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
fix(netex): stop the DSJ backfill from reporting provider job events (#839)

The batches that distribute the NeTEx exports of every provider to the legacy
and new DatedServiceJourney folders report an EXPORT_NETEX_LEGACY job event per
provider, built by JobEvent.providerJobBuilder from the exchange they run in.
Both batches run in a single exchange, so all these events carry the same
correlation id: the one of the aggregated export for
direct:distributeMissingDsjNetexExports, the one allocated by the admin endpoint
for direct:distributeAllDsjNetexExports.

Nabu aggregates timetable job events by correlation id alone and takes the
provider, the file name and the user of a job from the first event of the group.
The tst nightly run of 2026-09-16 therefore produced a single job out of the 92
events of the 46 providers distributed by the aggregated export: attributed to
rb_atb, without a file name, from 09:27:47 to 09:28:10. Ninkasi renders it as a
"Validation" row of AtB with every pipeline step greyed out, since it names a
job without a file name "Validation" and drops the actions that are not steps of
the import pipeline. Nothing was wrong with the run itself: the 46 providers
were distributed, the aggregated export completed and the graph build started.

A batch is a system action that belongs to no provider's import job: it now
reports nothing. The new PROP_REPORT_JOB_EVENTS property is cleared by the two
batch routes before the split, the way PROP_IGNORE_DISTRIBUTION_FAILURES already
is, and the four EXPORT_NETEX_LEGACY events are reported through
direct:reportDsjNetexExportJobEvent, which filters on it. That route also exists
so that the event is not built when it is not reported: JobEvent.build()
serialises the event into the body, and an event body that nobody publishes is
what #837 had to fix. The distribution itself is unchanged, and so is the
reporting of the publication pipeline, of the admin endpoint for a single
provider, which allocates its own correlation id, and of the blocks export.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
fix(netex): keep the blocks post-validation job event alive through the DSJ distribution (#837)

The EXPORT_NETEX_BLOCKS_POSTVALIDATION branch of direct:antuNetexValidationComplete
built its OK job event before calling direct:distributeDsjNetexBlocksExport, which
#833 added. JobEvent.build() serialises the event into the exchange body and
direct:updateStatus publishes the body and nothing else, but
direct:doDistributeDsjNetexBlocksExport blanks the body in its doFinally. Marduk
therefore published an empty message on JobEventQueue and Nabu never saw the OK
event: every block dataset validation stayed unfinished in Ninkasi, without a single
ERROR in the logs.

Build the event after the distribution instead, the way
ChouetteExportNetexBlocksRouteBuilder already does. It sits between the end of the
chouette.enablePostValidation filter and endChoice(), so that the event is still
produced when post-validation is enabled and the filtered block is skipped.

Also stop the two DSJ side routes from clobbering the exchange they are handed:
doDistributeDsjNetexBlocksExport and doDistributeOriginalDatasetToNisaba now save the
body and restore it in doFinally, exactly as they already do for FILE_HANDLE. A route
that is a no-op when the dual export is disabled should leave the exchange as it found
it when it is enabled.

Observed in dev after the nightly run of 2026-09-14: five providers reached
EXPORT_NETEX_BLOCKS_POSTVALIDATION/STARTED and none reached OK. tst and prd would have
lost the same events on their first nightly run after #833 was deployed, since
chouette.enablePostValidation=false and netex.dsj.enabled=true in all three
environments.

The regression went unnoticed because src/test/resources/application.properties leaves
chouette.enablePostValidation at its true default, which closes the filter and hides
the faulty path. The new test class sets it to false; a second test keeps the
flag-on variant covered.

Note: the OK event now carries the username "System" on untriggered runs, where it
previously carried none, because doDistributeDsjNetexBlocksExport defaults the
username and the event is built after it. Consistent with #834.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
feat(netex): keep the uploaded dataset before upgrading it to NeTEx 1.16 (#836)

The upgrade added by #833 replaces the stored dataset in place: direct:upgradeNetexDataset
downloads the blob at FILE_HANDLE, converts it and uploads the result to the same object.
The bytes the provider submitted are then gone, and there is no way back to them if the
XSLT turns out to mangle something or a provider disputes what was imported. #835 widened
the reach of that overwrite: the nightly validation runs the same upgrade, so a stored
dataset can be replaced months after its upload, with no upload event left to replay.

The dataset is now copied as it was uploaded before it is overwritten, next to the
upgraded one and under the same name postfixed by -original-v115
(inbound/received/rb_vyg/netex.zip -> inbound/received/rb_vyg/netex-original-v115.zip).
The copy is a server-side copy through direct:copyInternalBlobInBucket, taken while the
stored object still holds the original: the dataset is neither downloaded nor uploaded a
second time, and the body, the upgraded archive waiting to be uploaded, is untouched.

It is taken only when the upgrade actually converted a file, so a dataset already in
NeTEx 1.16, one of a codespace without replacement information and a non-NeTEx file leave
no copy - nothing was overwritten, so there is nothing to keep. It runs inside the doTry()
of the calling route, so a failed copy fails the upgrade before the original is
overwritten, which the nightly validation already reports as a failed PREVALIDATION.

The copy is a regular file of the provider's folder: it is listed and downloaded through
the timetable API like the dataset itself, and can be re-imported. A later upgrade of the
same dataset replaces it, so it always mirrors the dataset currently stored.

No new property: the copy is part of the upgrade step and is taken exactly when
netex.import.dsj.upgrade.enabled is set.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
fix(netex): upgrade the stored dataset to NeTEx 1.16 before the nightly validation (#835)

The NeTEx 1.16 upgrade added by #833 was wired into the upload path only:
direct:upgradeNetexDatasetIfNeeded had a single caller, direct:processValidFile.
The nightly validation reuses the dataset stored by the last upload
(NightlyValidationFileProcessor) and sends it straight to the validation bucket, so a
provider that has not uploaded since the pipeline moved to NeTEx 1.16 has its pre-1.16
dataset validated and re-imported as it is. For VYG, GOA and SJN that means Antu fails
the run on the deprecated DatedServiceJourneyRef, and on an Antu without that rule the
dataset reaches a NeTEx 1.16 Chouette, which drops every replacement reference silently.

The nightly validation now runs the same upgrade before copying the dataset to the
validation bucket, so the whole chain reads the upgraded dataset. The upgrade replaces
the stored dataset in place, so the first nightly run heals it and the following ones
convert nothing.

* the upgrade no longer requires a FILE_TYPE header. It is set by the classification of
  an uploaded file; the nightly validation reuses a stored dataset and never classifies
  it, and its candidates are not necessarily NeTEx providers. An absent header is
  therefore not a reason to skip the upgrade - the codespace decides - while a header
  naming another type still skips it.
* a dataset that cannot be upgraded fails that provider's nightly run and is reported as
  a failed pre-validation, rather than being validated as it is: falling back to the
  stored dataset is exactly the silent degradation the upgrade prevents. The other
  providers of the nightly run are unaffected.
* the failure is reported with doTry/doCatch rather than an onException on the nightly
  route: the exception is raised in another route, whose error handler marks the exchange
  as failure-handled before it returns, so the caller's failure processor never runs.
  rethrowCaughtException moves to BaseRouteBuilder, where both users can reach it.

Verified end to end on the local stack with the VYG dataset of 2026-09-11 (NeTEx 1.15,
25 839 DatedServiceJourneyRef) stored as the last uploaded file: before the change the
nightly run sent it unconverted and Antu failed it on the deprecated ref; after it, the
nightly upgraded all 25 files, Antu validated it with no error, the Chouette validation
and transfer jobs ran, and an import of the upgraded dataset left 25 839 replacement
references in Chouette.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
fix(netex): report the system as the user of an untriggered DSJ export (#834)

The job events of the DatedServiceJourney export carried no username when
no user triggered the export, and Ninkasi renders such an event as an empty
entry. This happens on every aggregated export: the OTP2 merged export
distributes the provider exports that are missing from the legacy or new
folder, and those exchanges carry no RutebankenUsername header.

Default the header to "System" on the two routes that report
EXPORT_NETEX_LEGACY events, the way the routes that fan out over all
providers in ChouetteValidationRouteBuilder already do. The header is only
filled in when it is absent, so an export triggered from the admin API,
which runs through direct:setUsername, is still reported as triggered by
that user.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
Dual NeTEx 1.15/1.16 export for the DatedServiceJourney transition (#833)

* feat(netex): dual NeTEx 1.15/1.16 export for the DatedServiceJourney transition

NeTEx 1.16 changes how a DatedServiceJourney references the journeys it replaces: the
additional DatedServiceJourneyRef elements become a replacedJourneys container holding
DatedVehicleJourneyRef. Chouette and Antu move to 1.16, but consumers of the published
datasets, OTP included, still read 1.15. Publish both versions from the same pipeline so
that each consumer migrates on its own schedule.

While netex.export.dsj.enabled is set, every published dataset is stored in three folders
of the public bucket: netex-dsj-new (as exported by the pipeline, 1.16), netex-dsj-legacy
(downgraded to 1.15) and the default folder netex, which receives the variant selected by
netex.export.dsj.default.variant. Phase 1 serves legacy from the default folder, phase 2
flips it to new, and the folders disappear once the transition is over. The private blocks
export and the original dataset sent to Nisaba are stored the same way; the timetable API
picks a variant with the dsjcompatibility request parameter.

Datasets uploaded by a provider are upgraded to 1.16 in place when
netex.import.dsj.upgrade.enabled is set, so that the import pipeline sees a single
version. Both conversions are XSLT transformations maintained in
no.rutebanken.marduk.netex.conversion; netex-java-model is only used by their tests, to
validate the converted documents against the schemas.

Only the codespaces listed in netex.dsj.codespaces produce DatedServiceJourneys with
replacement information (VYG, SJN, GOA); the datasets of the others are copied between the
folders unchanged. The conversions are selected on the version number declared by the
document rather than on a literal prefix, since these codespaces publish a spread of
versions: the upgrade converts everything older than 1.16 and the downgrade everything
newer than 1.15.

* fix(netex): fail the publication instead of silently skipping a DSJ variant

Review follow-up on the dual NeTEx 1.15/1.16 export.

A failed distribution was swallowed in three places, each leaving one
folder silently out of step with the others:

* the per-provider backfill skipped a provider whose export could not be
  distributed, and the aggregated Norway export was then built from a
  folder missing that provider and copied into the default folder, which
  is also the OTP graph input. The backfill now only tolerates a failure
  when it is not feeding an aggregated export, and every variant of the
  aggregated export is checked to cover the same providers as the
  previous one.
* the original dataset sent to Nisaba: the imported/ copy is written by
  that route alone, so swallowing the failure left the import without an
  original dataset for good.
* the NeTEx blocks export: the legacy copy is overwritten in place and
  the timetable API cannot tell a stale copy from a current one, so a
  swallowed failure made it serve the previous run's dataset as current.

convertZip now rejects a source holding no entry, which otherwise
produced an empty archive silently.

Documentation: "legacy" names the DatedServiceJourney replacement
structure, not the NeTEx version of the dataset. A dataset without
replacement information is copied between the folders unchanged and keeps
the version the pipeline exported, which is NeTEx 1.16 once Chouette has
migrated; the OpenAPI description, the dsjcompatibility parameter, the
folder javadoc and the README all claimed otherwise. Also drops FLT from
the codespace list in the README and the stale netex-java-model
attribution for the converters, which now live in marduk.

* chore(helm): enable the NeTEx 1.16 upgrade on import in every environment

Chouette and Antu move to NeTEx 1.16 when this PR is merged, so rollout
step 2 is configured together with step 1: uploaded datasets of the
DatedServiceJourney codespaces that still declare a version older than
1.16 are upgraded in place, and the pipeline sees a single NeTEx version.

* fix(netex): resolve the configured DatedServiceJourney variants at startup

netex.export.dsj.api.default.variant was only read while serving a
download, and outside the try/catch of resolveApiVariant, so an
unparseable value started normally and then turned every dataset download
into a 400 naming no property. The same typo in
netex.export.dsj.default.variant aborted the context at boot instead,
because the route builder reads it while building routes.

Both are now resolved once in a @PostConstruct and fail the context with a
message naming the property at fault. parseVariant is package-private so
that the parsing is unit-tested directly rather than through a context
that refuses to start.

commits.author: Vincent Paturet
commits.message:
feat(otp2): publish the new graph under a stable name per serialization version (#832)

In addition to the timestamped graph file and the pointer files, copy the published OTP2 graph
to netex-otp2/<serialization version>/Graph-otp2-current.obj. OTP instances can then load the
graph for their own serialization version directly (OTP substitutes
${otp.serialization.version.id} in build-config.json) instead of resolving the pointer file in
an entrypoint script, which lets the OTP image run without a shell.

The copy happens before the pointer files are written, since those trigger the redeployment of
the OTP instances. The stable copy is excluded from the graph listing (Otp2ListGraphRouteBuilder)
because it duplicates the timestamped file.

commits.message:
Move the readiness probe off the application port (#831)

camel-kubernetes derives cluster membership from pod readiness, so a stall on
platform-http's shared task executor could drop a pod out of the cluster and
flap leadership. Also raises renew-deadline-millis, which is what expired on
the leader before the 2026-09-01 flap. Neither is proven to explain the
RejectedExecutionException storm that followed.

commits.author: henrik242
commits.message:
Poll the graph builder job status when the pod watch stalls (#828)

A fabric8 pod watch can stop delivering events without raising an error, so
runJob() blocked on a latch that was never released and wedged the graph build
route for the whole timeout. Poll the job status every 60s as a backstop and
log a warning when the poll, not the watch, detects the terminal state.

Cut the timeout from 12000 to 5400. Observed builds are 16-20 minutes for
netex and 18-32 for base.

commits.author: Henrik Brautaset Aronsen
commits.message:
Harden the docker smoke gate and drop a dead RBAC rule

IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions keeps the chart deployable against a pre-JDK-24
image, where --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access does not exist and kills the
launcher before any log line. The smoke job now reads the options with yq and
asserts on them, so a broken lift fails instead of silently running the image
with no flags, and it gates docker-push rather than docker-build. Leader
election uses a Lease, so the marduk-leaders configmaps grant was dead.
